```{r}
library(fpp2)
library(forecast)
library(readxl)
busineesforecasting_us_average_prices_monthly <-read_excel("busineesforecasting_us_average_prices_monthly.xlsx")
eggs <- subset (busineesforecasting_us_average_prices_monthly, grepl("egg", item, ignore.case=TRUE))
class(eggs)
ts_eggs <-ts(eggs$price,start = c(2015,1),frequency = 12)
plot(ts_eggs)
#Downloading the dataset and creating the time series egg subset.


ndiffs(ts_eggs)
#Output is 1 so the series requires 1 difference before modeling 
tsdisplay(ts_eggs)
ts_eggsdiff1 <- diff(ts_eggs, differences=1)
plot(ts_eggsdiff1)
tsdisplay(ts_eggsdiff1)

auto_fit <- auto.arima(ts_eggs, trace=TRUE, stepwise = FALSE)
auto_fit
#AIC= 28.97 : strong balance between goodness of fit and model complexity. Sigma^2 = 0.06896 is small and suggests that the model captures most of the variation in the data

attributes(auto_fit)
plot(forecast(auto_fit,h=5,level=c(99.5)))

# 5 Ways to do Residual Analysis
Acf(auto_fit$residuals)
#All of the ACF lines are within the significance bounds. This suggests that little autocorrelation remains.  

Box.test(residuals(auto_fit), lag=20, type="Ljung")
#The p-value = 0.8264 > 0.05. The box test was not significant and suggests there is no evidence of autocorrelation remaining.

plot.ts(residuals(auto_fit))
#Shows the residuals are centered around zero and have no systematic trend or seasonal pattern. 

hist(auto_fit$residuals)
#Most residuals are centered around zero and there is a roughly bell-shaped distribution.

tsdiag(auto_fit)
#Standardized residuals: fluctuate randomly around zero
#ACF of residuals: Shows all autocorrelation values fall within the significance
#p-values for Ljung-Box Statistic: All are greater than 0.05 across the lags
#All indicate there is no autocorrelation remaining in the residuals and supports the ARIMA model.

#Seasonal Data
plot(euretail)
nsdiffs(euretail)
ndiffs(euretail)
ndiffs((diff(euretail,4)))
tsdisplay(diff(diff(euretail,4)))
fit3 <- auto.arima(euretail,trace=TRUE, stepwise = FALSE )
fit3
#There is one regular difference and one seasonal difference to remove trend and quarterly seasonality. Three moving average terms and one seasonal moving average term were included to capture short-term and seasonal dependencies in the data. AIC = 67.26 and Sigma^2 = 0.156 suggesting a strong fit while maintaining model parsimony.

#Residual Analysis
Acf(fit3$residuals)
#All residual auto correlations are within the 95% confidence bounds. No statistically significant autocorrelation remains in the residuals, which suggests the model captured both the trend and seasonal components. 

Box.test(residuals(fit3), lag=20, type="Ljung")
#P-value = 0.9951 > 0.05. The null hypothesis of independent residuals can't be rejected. It suggests there are no significant auto correlation remaining in the residuals. 

plot.ts(residuals(fit3))
#No apparent trend/seasonal behavior. Suggests that the model has successfully captured the underlying trend and seasonal components. There are a few larger residuals but they appear to be isolated.

hist(fit3$residuals)
#Centered around zero and bell shaped, generally unbiased and normally distributed. 

tsdiag(fit3)
#Standardized residuals: most fall between -2 and 2. Randomly distributed 
#ACF: Within the blue confidence bounds
#Ljung-Box p-values: Above the significance line

#Accuracy models
accuracy(auto_fit)
#RMSE = 0.2578, lower RMSE indicates better predictive performance. MAE = 0.1770, small forecast error. MAPE = 7.25%, models forecasts differ from actual values. MASE = 0.2133. ACF1= 0.0601

accuracy(fit3)
#RMSE = 0.3661 and MAE = 0.279, indicates small forecast errors. MAPE = 0.289 suggesting high forecast accuracy. MASE = 0.227, ACF1 = 0.006
```
